text:
Tyler Bertuzzi scored 32 goals for Chicago last season, and this year's version has been slower to arrive. He has 6 goals and 14 points in 24 games, but most of it came lately: eight points in his last ten, including two goals and an assist in the win over Toronto on November 17 and three points in Saturday's 6-3 win over Vancouver. The Athletic's Mark Lazerus noted the Blackhawks are 4-1-1 since the loss in Carolina, with the power play "red hot". Bertuzzi sits on the top unit, and six of his points have come with the man advantage.

At 5v5 the picture is rough. Chicago takes 42% of the expected goals with him on the ice, which says more about the team than about him; Evolving-Hockey had his linemates in the bottom 1% by impact last season while his own effect sat at the 90th percentile, 20th among forwards in wins above replacement.

His shooting (18%) is in his normal range, and his points rate matches what we think he is. The net-front work (he screened the goalie on Frank Nazar's 11th goal) is the part that never shows in a box score.
